lesson.title: Hello Python!
lesson.driving_question: How can a Python program ask for input and display a message?
lesson.concept_budget: Store text input in variables and display it with print().
misconceptions: The equal sign stores a value in a variable.
input() returns the text entered by the user.
print() can display several values in order.
lesson.progression_note: Introduces the input-process-output pattern used throughout the suite.

shared_program.code:
name = input("What is your name? ")

print("Hello,", name, "!")

primm.prompt: Identify the input, variable and output in the example program.
Predict the complete message when the user enters a name.
Run the supplied file and compare the output with your prediction.

questions: What does the equal sign do?
What creates the green string literals?
How does print() combine several values?

primm.prompt: Create a variable called greeting and store a greeting in another language, such as "Xin chao". Change print() so it displays the greeting, the user's name and an exclamation mark.
Ask for the user's name and a friend's name. Display "Hello, [name] and [friend]!" using both answers.
Create a new program that asks for two school subjects. Display the message "I think [subject 1] and [subject 2] are great subjects!" using the two answers.
Repair the quotation marks, input call and variable name.

blocks.definition: Storing a value in a variable with the equal sign (=).
Receiving text entered by the user with input().
Displaying information for the user with print().
A collection of text characters inside quotation marks.
A name used to store and access information.

slides.body: This code has errors! Look closely at the code to find the problems:

programs.challenge1:
name = input("What is your name? ")
greeting = "Xin chao"

print(greeting, name, "!")
programs.challenge2:
name = input("What is your name? ")
friend_name = input("What is your friend's name? ")

print("Hello,", name, "and", friend_name, "!")
programs.challenge3:
subject_1 = input("What subject do you study in school? ")
subject_2 = input("What is another subject you study in school? ")

print("I think", subject_1, "and", subject_2, "are great subjects!")
programs.broken:
# Lesson 01 - Hello Python!
# Fix the code!

name = input(What is your name?)
sport = print("What is your favorite sport?")

print("Hmmmmm")
print("Today I learned", name, "really likes", favSport, "!")
programs.fixed:
# Lesson 01 - Hello Python!
# Fix the code! - Solution

name = input("What is your name?") #Use quotation marks for text/strings
sport = input("What is your favorite sport?") #Use input instead of print

print("Hmmmmm")
print("Today I learned", name, "really likes", sport, "!") #Use matching variable names - sport instead of favSport
